Description: v1 (mache-eb2bf3, ley-line-open-ea1e42). Every backtick-fenced Rust path `pkg::Item` cited in markdown should resolve to a real definition in node_defs; a missing definition signals the doc has drifted from the code (renamed/removed item still referenced in docs). SCOPED TO RUST PATHS (token LIKE '%::%') for v1, not every backtick span: ley-line-open-651909 is open (Go package-level consts emit no defs, qualified selector arguments emit no refs), and Go doesn't use '::', so this scoping sidesteps that gap entirely rather than producing Go false positives — measured, a generic node_refs-vs-node_defs join on mache's own docs flagged .db, [], bead IDs, model names, and file paths as 'dead symbols' before this scoping. MATCHING: a def token can equal the ref's full qualified token (Rust sometimes indexes methods as Type::method directly) OR its bare last segment (Rust more commonly indexes free functions/types by bare name, so `epic::is_dominated_by` must resolve against a def token of just `is_dominated_by` — verified empirically: the qualified form never matches directly, only the bare segment does). Trailing `()` call syntax is stripped before matching. TWO KNOWN FALSE-POSITIVE CLASSES, both left unfiltered rather than papered over with a fragile allowlist: (1) EXTERNAL REFERENCES — a citation of an external crate's API (`std::fs::read_to_string`, `serde_json::Value`, `capnp::serialize::write_message`) is indistinguishable from a real internal rename without a crate registry this rule doesn't have; (2) ENUM VARIANTS AND STRUCT FIELDS — `Type::Variant` / `Type::field` shaped citations frequently have no node_defs row at all (extraction currently indexes functions/types/consts, not variants or fields), which is the Rust-side sibling of the Go const gap this rule was scoped to avoid. Measured on mache's own docs + the medium-rust-rosary test fixture: 13 candidates total, and by inspection every one falls into class (1) or (2) — none confirmed as genuine drift. A human reading a finding from this rule should check both classes before treating it as real. No position data: node_refs carries no byte/row/col columns, and LLO's injection fold deliberately emits no _ast rows for injected markdown subtrees (that's what keeps host file hashes independent of the injected grammar), so there is nowhere to source an exact span from — start_byte/end_byte/start_row/start_col report 0, same as the placeholder this replaces. Not tagged 'gate': advisory only, not part of the smell ratchet.
Query:
SELECT v.source_id AS source_id,
			       v.node_id AS node_id,
			       0 AS start_byte,
			       0 AS end_byte,
			       0 AS start_row,
			       0 AS start_col,
			       0 AS metric
			FROM v_doc_refs v
			WHERE NOT EXISTS (
				-- A def matches the ref either by its full qualified token (some
				-- Rust method defs are indexed Type::method directly) or by the
				-- bare last segment (free functions/types are more commonly
				-- indexed by bare name — verified empirically: a qualified
				-- module-path citation like 'epic::is_dominated_by' never matches
				-- directly, only the bare 'is_dominated_by' segment does).
				SELECT 1 FROM node_defs nd
				WHERE nd.token = v.token
				   OR nd.token = v.bare
				   OR v.bare LIKE '%%::' || nd.token
			)
			%s
			ORDER BY source_id, node_id
